title: A Microfluidic System with Surface Patterning for Investigating Cavitation Bubble(s)–Cell Interaction and the Resultant Bioeffects at the Single-cell Level
protocol: Flush the glass slide with acetone followed by isopropyl alcohol (IPA), and then dry it with N2 flow.
Soak the slide in piranha solution (H2SO4:H2O2 = 4:1) for 10 min.
Rinse the slide with DI water, and then dry it with N2 flow.
Bake the glass slide on a hotplate at 120 °C for 10 min.
Treat the slide in a plasma asher at 100 W for 90 s.
Turn on a hotplate and wait until the temperature is stable at 95 °C.
Fix the cleaned glass slide onto the spin coater by applying vacuum.
Cover the slide surface with P-20 and start the coating recipe.
Bake the slide at 95 °C for 60 s.
Mount the chrome mask onto the mask aligner with pattern side facing down.
Set the photolithography recipe to hard exposure mode with 9 s of UV exposure.
Align the glass substrate with the mask.
Bake the slide at 95 °C for 1 min after UV exposure.
Develop the pattern on the slide in developer solution for 60 s.
Remove the slide from the developer and flush it with DI water.
Dry the slide with N2 flow.
Check the pattern geometry under a microscope.
Measure and record the feature size.
Bake the slide at 120 °C for 5 min.
Clean the slide with plasma in the reactive ion etching (RIE) machine for 90 s at 500 Torr and 100 W.
Deposit 5 nm of Ti onto the slide using an E-beam evaporator.
Deposit 15 nm of Au onto the slide using an E-beam evaporator.
Soak the slide overnight in photoresist remover solvent.
Flush the slide with acetone followed by IPA.
Dry the slide with N2 flow.
Dry the slide on a hot plate at 115 °C.
Clean the slide in the oxygen plasma asher at 100 W for 90 s.
Use S1813-positive photoresist and set temperature to 115 °C.
Mount the chrome mask onto the mask aligner with pattern side down towards the slide.
Set photolithography recipe to hard exposure mode with 9 seconds of UV exposure.
Align top mask with bottom slide using alignment marks as a spatial reference.
Verify that the pattern features are aligned correctly in the central portion of the mask.
Complete the UV exposure without post-bake.
Repeat development step but with 45 seconds of development before drying on hotplate.
Preserve the slide in N2 storage.
Prepare the passivating solution: Mix 0.5 mg/mL PLL-g-PEG in 10 mM HEPES buffer.
Retrieve the slide from N2 storage.
Clean the slide using RIE with a pressure of 500 Torr, power of 100 W, and duration of 90 seconds.
Pipette one drop of passivating solution onto a piece of paraffin film.
Sandwich the solution between the film and the slide with the side containing pattern features facing down; avoid bubble formation.
Wait for 45 minutes before removing the slide from the film.
Soak the slide in photoresist remover, followed by photoresist remover and DI water (1:1) mixture, then in DI water alone.
Agitate each soak in an ultrasound bath for 90 seconds.
Dry the slide on a hotplate to remove moisture.
Seal the slide in a desiccator and store it in a refrigerator.
Repeat steps for chip assembly using SU8-2025-negative photoresist according to the Microchem protocol.
Fabricate a PDMS microchannel (40 mm x 25 mm x 5 mm) and a small PDMS slab (800 µm-wide groove structure).
Punch fluid access ports in the microchannel.
Clean the microchannel with tape and IPA.
Shield the patterned area of the glass substrate with the PDMS slab.
Apply RIE (100 W, 500 mTorr, 60 s) to remove PLL-g-PEG from the peripheral area.
Treat the microchannel with a reduced dose of RIE (25 W, 500 mTorr, 25 s).
Align the treated microchannel to the patterned glass substrate after removing the small PDMS slab.
Bring the microchannel and the patterned glass substrate into conformal contact under a stereoscope.
Prime the chip with PBS for 30 min at 1 µL/min.
Infuse fibronectin solution (50 µg/mL in PBS) for 45 min at 1 µL/min.
Trypsinize cell culture with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA while waiting.
Wash cells in culture medium after trypsinization.
Centrifuge individual cells.
Reconstitute the cell suspension in pre-warmed (37 °C) culture medium at a concentration of 5x10^6 cells/mL.
Replace the fibronectin solution with PBS and flush the chip for 5 min at 10 µL/min.
Inject the prepared cell suspension into the chip.
Stop the flow and clamp the outlet.
Maintain the chip in a cell culture incubator for 30 min.
Release the outlet and flush the chip with cell culture medium at 10 µL/min for 5 min.
Reduce the perfusion flow rate of the culture medium to 0.75 µL/min.
Maintain the cell culture for 2 h in the incubator.
Place the microfluidic chip on the stage of an inverted microscope.
Align the foci of two pulsed Nd:YAG lasers (λ = 532 nm, 5-ns pulse duration) on a pair of patterned gold dots separated by 40 µm.
Trigger the two lasers with a time delay about 2.5 µs to produce tandem bubbles initiated at the gold dots.
Adjust the laser output energy (~10 µJ) to produce a maximum diameter of the bubbles within 50 ± 2 µm.
Synchronize a high-speed camera (200-ns exposure and 2 million frames per second (fps)) to the lasers.
Capture the dynamics of bubble expansion, collapse, bubble-bubble interaction, and jet formation.
Record the position of the jet tip (J1) at the proximal end of the first bubble (B1).
Record the position of the distal end of B1 starting at the generation of the second bubble (B2).
End recording when J1 touches down towards the distal end of B1.
Linearly fit the time course of position for both the proximal and distal ends.
Calculate the slope of the tip position versus time curve to determine the jet speed.
Determine the intersection of the two lines to indicate the jet touchdown time.
Prepare a 1 µm polystyrene (PS) bead suspension in DI water at 2.6% w/v.
Inject the PS beads into the microfluidic chip.
Generate tandem bubbles as described previously.
Record the tandem bubble dynamics using a high-speed video camera at 5 M fps with a 100-ns exposure time.
Upload image sequence into commercial PIV software.
Divide each image into smaller interrogation windows of 16 x 16 pixels with a 75% overlap.
Apply multi-pass iteration and regional filters to reduce velocity field computation errors.
Output results in a velocity vector map.
Replace the regular culture medium with PI solution running at a perfusion flow rate of 0.5 µL/min throughout the experiment.
Program the microscope control software to automatically select the PI fluorescent cube on the rotating turret.
Synchronize the timing of the CCD camera with the PI fluorescence excitation to capture fluorescence images.
Set the exposure time for capturing fluorescence images to 200 ms.
Record both bright field and fluorescence images before the tandem bubble treatment.
Start a time-lapse fluorescence image recording immediately after step 2.1 to capture PI uptake history.
Prepare 1-µm beads at a concentration of 1% w/v, activated with water-soluble carbodiimide.
Functionalize the prepared beads with Peptide-2000 at a concentration of 100 µg/mL in PBS.
Incubate attached cells with functionalized beads at a density of 1x10^9 beads/mL at 37°C for 30 min.
Identify a triad of three beads that remain on the imaging plane throughout the experiment.
Compile the positions (x1, y1), (x2, y2), and (x3, y3) of the identified beads in the experiment coordinates.
Calculate the area of the bead triad before the tandem bubble treatment.
Calculate the area of the bead triad after the tandem bubble treatment.
Calculate the area strain using the formula provided.
Based on the coordinates of three vertices before and after the tandem bubble treatment, calculate the local principal strain following established protocols.
Record the position of each treated cell in the microfluidic channel while repeating step 3.1.
Incubate the treated cells in the cell culture medium for another 2 h before perfusing the chip with FITC Annexin V solution for 15 min.
Repeat step 3.3.2 24 h after the tandem bubble treatment to study the long-term bioeffects in the targeted cells.
Mix 3 μL of fura-2 AM stock solution (1 mg/mL in DMSO) with 3 μL of 10% w/v Pluronic F-127 in 500 μL of reduced serum medium to prepare the final labeling solution (6 µM).
Replace the cell culture medium with the labelling solution and incubate under room temperature in the dark for 40 min.
Refill the channel with the reduced serum medium before starting the cell experiment.
Start ratiometric imaging (wavelength: 340/380 nm, 50-ms exposure) of the target cell using the commercial PTI system.
After 10 seconds of ratiometric imaging of the cell at resting level, produce tandem bubbles as in step 2.1.
Record with an interframe time (IFT) of 0.1 seconds for 1 minute.
Increase the IFT to 1 second and record for another minute.
Further increase the IFT to 5 seconds and continue recording.
Use the PTI software to calculate the ratio R = F340/F380 in the region of interest (ROI).
